articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although learning design (LD) plays a central role in shaping online courses, large-scale empirical evidence on how courses are actually structured remains scarce, and existing analytics work has characterised courses through student engagement with specific learning activities rather than through indicators of the design itself. articles.title: OpenHamoye: A Multi-Scale Open Geospatial Intelligence Framework for Decision Support Across Nigeria
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision-making in urban planning, infrastructure prioritization and commercial strategy benefits from granular spatial information. In Nigeria, official statistics are often published at coarse scales and with temporal lag. We present OpenHamoye, an open geospatial intelligence framework that integrates nine public remote-sensing and crowd-sourced datasets into reproducible, multi-scale proxy indicators for development conditions across Nigeria. articles.title: Governing Artificial Intelligence as a Macro Socio-Technical Regime: The F-I-C-P Framework for Regime-Level AI Infrastructure and Governance
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often analysed through technical, organisational, or regulatory perspectives that treat capability, adoption, and governance as separate issues. This article conceptualises AI instead as an emerging macro socio-technical regime generated through the interaction of finance, infrastructure, capability, and productivity. articles.title: LLM-as-a-Judge Version Shift: The Instrument Changed, Not the Standard
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated research pipelines increasingly rely on fixed LLM judges to rank, filter, and revise proposals, yet these judges are routinely replaced by newer versions. We study whether such replacements preserve the underlying measurement standard. Using a preregistered, frozen-weight design, we evaluate three adjacent same-family transitions across Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral on frozen ML research proposals under randomized information conditions. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly deliver information through personas, but it is unclear whether correcting the facts also makes their framing consistent across identity labels. articles.title: A pedagogically guided LLM framework for scaffolding human-AI cocreation and preserving learners' agency and creativity
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate alternatives, elaborate ideas and supply rationales, overlapping with cognitive work learners are expected to perform. articles.title: Learning by Collaborating in the Age of AI: Research Mentorship for Polymathic, Workflow-Centered Science
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.34606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how data-driven research is produced. articles.title: Cheap AI-Assisted Reverse Engineering and What It Will Do
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.35633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI is putting the law of reverse engineering (RE) under severe strain. Existing IP and technology laws assume that RE is expensive and time-consuming, and that it requires specialized expertise. They generally allow it, but they rely on its difficulty as a filter to separate (permissible) RE from (impermissible) copying and theft.
